sourceOpenUnits.requirement: **2. Grip the vessel wall and exit.** A T cell in a fast-flowing vessel first rolls along the wall, then sticks firmly using adhesion molecules, then squeezes between the lining cells ([Slaney et al., 2014](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25477332/)). Tumor vessels are often leaky and disorganized, and their lining may show little of the adhesion molecules intercellular adhesion molecule 1 (ICAM-1) and vascular cell adhesion molecule 1 (VCAM-1). In mouse and human melanoma models, CXCR3 signaling was needed for transferred CD8 T cells to stick inside tumor vessels and leave them ([Mikucki et al., 2015](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26109379/)).
sourceOpenUnits.residual: The low ICAM-1/VCAM-1 tumour-vessel clause needs an appropriate read passage.
